description: HIPAA-aligned healthcare API framework layer — Drizzle schema (patients, encounters, providers, immutable audit_logs), PHI field-level encryption, PHI-access middleware.

buildHints.whenToUse: Healthcare products, clinical platforms, patient portals, EHR/EMR integrations, or any service that stores or transmits Protected Health Information (PHI) and requires HIPAA-compliant infrastructure from day one.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then set `DATABASE_URL` (postgres://...) and `PHI_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (64-char hex: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"`).
Run `pnpm db:generate && pnpm db:migrate` to create the patients, encounters, providers, and audit_logs tables.
Start the server with `pnpm dev` — it listens on port 8100. `GET /health` should return `{"status":"ok"}`.
All `/api/*` routes require `X-Actor-Id` and `X-Actor-Role` headers; wire in your real auth layer (better-auth or Clerk slot) before storing real PHI.
Run `node validate-hipaa.mjs` to verify all required HIPAA controls are present.
dataModels: Patient (mrn, encryptedName, encryptedDob, encryptedSsn, sex, createdAt)
Encounter (patientId, providerId, encounteredAt, encryptedNotes, cptCode, icd10Codes)
AuditLog (actorId, action, resourceType, resourceId, occurredAt, reason) — append-only
integrations: Node crypto (AES-256-GCM) for field-level PHI encryption
Append-only audit_logs via trigger / INSERT-only grants
architectureNotes: PHI is never stored in plaintext — encrypted columns use AES-256-GCM with per-record IV
Every PHI read goes through phi-access middleware which writes an AuditLog row BEFORE returning data
audit_logs is append-only: no UPDATE/DELETE grants in production; enforced by Postgres trigger
Encryption key comes from PHI_ENCRYPTION_KEY env — in production this lives in a KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault)
gotchas: NEVER log PHI to stdout, stderr, files, or APM traces — logging middleware must redact patient.name, patient.dob, encounter.notes. Console.log of a Patient row is a HIPAA breach.
A BAA (Business Associate Agreement) with every subprocessor (cloud provider, email, analytics, error tracking) is REQUIRED before storing real PHI. Test data only until BAAs are executed.
audit_logs must be append-only. Do NOT add .update() / .delete() helpers on the AuditLog table — the whole point is tamper-evidence.
AES-256-GCM requires a UNIQUE IV per encryption. Reusing IV + key on different plaintexts breaks confidentiality. The helper generates a random 12-byte IV per field.
Don't store the encryption key in the database, source code, or the same secret store as the DB creds. Key compromise + DB compromise = total PHI exposure.
HIPAA minimum-necessary rule: API responses must filter fields based on the caller's role. A billing user doesn't need to see encounter.notes.
PHI must be encrypted in transit — TLS 1.2+ only. Disable HTTP. Disable weak ciphers.
Audit log retention is 6 years minimum under HIPAA. Lifecycle policy on object storage, NOT ad-hoc deletes.

placeholders.description: resolveActor reads X-Actor-Id / X-Actor-Role headers as a stub. Replace with your real auth layer (Clerk, better-auth, mTLS) before storing real PHI.
